title: Eval Watchtower: Console alert fanout and suppression bridge for model/config change regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When a model or configuration change triggers eval regressions, ops and on-call receive noisy, duplicate alerts across Slack channels and PagerDuty. This causes alert fatigue and slow incident triage for customer-impacting regressions.

Goal: Implement an Eval Watchtower layer in Console that acts as a bridge between Evals change detectors and downstream notification channels. The Watchtower should: 1) smartly fan out important regression notices to Slack and PagerDuty, 2) suppress or group duplicates across short time windows, 3) surface root-cause hints (model vs. config change), and 4) allow per-team routing and escalation policies.

Scope: Console UI and routing config, alert dedupe/suppression heuristics, Slack/PagerDuty integrations, short-term datastore for dedupe fingerprints, observability for false-positive/false-negative tracking. Backend work will be in the evals-notice service and a small routing microservice (watchtower-bridge).

Success metrics: Reduce duplicate Slack messages by >= 75% for the first 24h after a model/config rollout; decrease PagerDuty noise by 60% while preserving mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for high-severity regressions; telemetry to show accurate grouping vs. manual ungrouping events.

Non-goals: Replacing on-call escalation logic (keep PagerDuty severity mapping intact), building a full-blown RCA engine (we only surface heuristics and links to detailed diffs).

Design summary:
- Ingest: Evals change detector produces a compact notice (change_id, model_version, config_hash, sample set id, metric deltas, confidence score, provenance links).
- Fingerprint: Normalize key fields and compute a dedupe fingerprint using (model_version or model_alias, config_hash, root_prompt_hash, top-N failing tests signature).
- Temporal grouping: Sliding window default 30 minutes; configurable per-project 5-240 minutes. Notices with matching fingerprint collapse into a single thread.
- Confidence and severity mapping: Use confidence score + magnitude delta to decide Slack thread (info/warning/critical) and PagerDuty routing (only critical or customer-impacting) unless manually escalated.
- Channel fanout: Post a single Slack thread message per fingerprint with concise summary + link to eval diff dashboard. Tag teams from model owners mapping in Console. Only the first critical notice triggers PagerDuty. Subsequent deduped critical notices suppress PD but update the existing rerouted thread.
- Manual override: Console UI to force re-fanout, ungroup, or escalate to PagerDuty; history shows suppressed notices and who un-suppressed them.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong grouping reduces noise but risks hiding distinct regressions if fingerprinting is too coarse. We will start conservative (fingerprint includes prompt hash and failing test signature) and iterate.
- Storing fingerprints for dedupe increases storage and retention costs; initial TTL 48 hours for fingerprints (configurable) and metrics kept for 30 days.
- Slack threads vs new messages: threads preserve context but may be missed by teams that monitor channels rather than threads. We'll include channel tagging and ephemeral escalation pings when a thread reaches a severity threshold.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal-only for infra and internal model teams (2 weeks) to validate dedupe heuristics.
2) Beta: enable opt-in per-customer/project with telemetry (4 weeks).
3) GA: default on for hosted customers with opt-out for noisy teams (post-telemetry).

Monitoring & telemetry: Track grouped_count, suppressed_count, PD_escalations, Slack_thread_responses, manual_unmutes, false_group_reports (from UI). Dashboards: console.redwood.ai/evals/watchtower and an ops Grafana board.

Open questions:
- Should we allow cross-project grouping when the same model serves multiple projects? (initial answer: opt-in via project-level toggle)
- How to surface suggested model substitutions in the thread? (defer to evals team roadmap)

Artifacts: design doc, figma mockups, initial API contract, telemetry plan.
